rules.description: A 'free bar': the whole bar sits outside the Keltner band — the low is above the upper band (long) / the high below the lower band (short). Grimes's sign of a climactic, unsustainable imbalance.

complexity.reason: the same EMA/ATR band, tested against the bar's extreme rather than its close

catalog_match.note: EmaGapBar is low > emaVal with no band; add marginAtr (2.25) and atrLookback (20) to it exactly as CloseBeyondEma adds them to the close test. At marginAtr 0 it is today's EmaGapBar, so every existing placement is unchanged

rules.merge_notes: Three identical restatements, all on low/high rather than close, so kept apart from CloseOutsideKeltnerBand: the entire bar must clear the band. The cheapest authoring is the one input pair on EmaGapBar named above, not a new rule file.

rules.description: Riding the band: at least rideCount of the last rideLookback bars (ending `lag` bars ago) closed beyond the Keltner band on the trade's side — a one-sided market that never pulls back to the average.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(close[k + lag] > ema(close, emaLength)[k + lag] + bandMult * atr(atrLength)[k + lag], rideLookback) >= rideCount

complexity.reason: a CountIF over the band test, which needs the EMA's own lagged history mirrored as a ring buffer (EmaSlope's precedent)

catalog_match.note: identical count shape, but that rule counts closes beyond the bare EMA while this counts closes beyond the ATR band — a far rarer event, so the two are not the same bars at any shared parameters

rules.merge_notes: G03-21's riding-the-band and G05-02's 'multiple free bars' (which counts closes, not whole bars) are one counter; G05-02 is this rule at rideCount = rideLookback. No book numbers; 5 of 10 chosen. `lag` is added so a pane can AND the run-as-of-the-prior-bar with a negated CloseBeyondEma, which reconstructs G05-03.

rules.description: At least freeBarCount of the last freeBarLookback bars were free bars (the whole bar outside the band) — Grimes's 'many free bars' climax marker.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(low[k] > ema(close, emaLength)[k] + bandMult * atr(atrLength)[k], freeBarLookback) >= freeBarCount

complexity.reason: a CountIF over the free-bar test, with the EMA's lagged history mirrored

catalog_match.note: ConsecutiveClimaxBarCount counts large trend bars against an ATR, not bars outside a band; no overlap at any parameters

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from ClosesOutsideKeltnerBandCount: free bars test low/high, that rule tests closes. The book gives no count ('many'), so both window and threshold are optimizer inputs.

rules.description: While the market has pressed into either Keltner band for rideCount of the last rideWindow bars, take no new position on either side — Grimes's 'difficult trading environment' override.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(close[k] > upperBand[k], rideWindow) >= rideCount OR countIf(close[k] < lowerBand[k], rideWindow) >= rideCount

complexity.reason: two CountIFs over the band test; the OR of the two sides is what makes it a Switch rather than a mirrored filter

catalog_match.note: same role and intent — a global block — on the opposite condition: that rule blocks in an unusually tight range, this one in an unusually one-sided market

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from ClosesOutsideKeltnerBandCount by ROLE, on the RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple / TightRangeBlocksEntries precedent: an OR of both sides cannot be built from ANDed directional panes. Same divergence to record: the generator's Switch also forces flat, which Grimes does not ask for.

rules.description: Within a short window the market has closed beyond BOTH Keltner bands — a sharp move one way immediately reversed the other — so expect consolidation and take no new position.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(close[k] > upperBand[k], spikeLookback) >= 1 AND countIf(close[k] < lowerBand[k], spikeLookback) >= 1

complexity.reason: two window scans over the band test; no position state

catalog_match.note: same 'both directions spiked inside one window, so expect sideways' idea, measured against the Keltner bands rather than against two large opposite trend bars

rules.merge_notes: Not composable: an AND of an upper-band read and a lower-band read cannot be built from mirrored directional panes, and two Switch placements OR rather than AND. The mined cooldownBars is folded into spikeLookback — one window, default 10.

rules.description: The original Chester Keltner channel: the close is beyond a simple average of the typical price (H+L+C)/3 offset by a multiple of the average bar RANGE (not ATR).
rules.pseudocode: close[0] > average((high + low + close) / 3, maLength)[0] + bandMult * average(high - low, rangeLength)[0]

complexity.reason: two fresh Averages over price expressions; EL's Average recomputes from scratch every bar, so no warm-up mirroring is needed

catalog_match.note: that rule is Average(close) +/- ATR tested as a cross; this is Average(typical price) +/- average RANGE tested as a state. Three differences — centre series, band series, cross vs state — so not the same bars at any parameters

rules.merge_notes: Glossary-only, and the one place Grimes states the pre-modification indicator. bandMult is unspecified by the book; 1.0 chosen. Range averaging, unlike ATR, ignores gaps, which is the whole behavioural difference from the corpus's ATR bands.
